label: Frankforter
summary: American chemist (1859-1947), professor and first dean of the School of Chemistry at the University of Minnesota.

label: Frary
summary: American chemical engineer (1884-1970), later long-time director of research at Alcoa.

label: Michaux (Mchx.)
summary: French botanist (1770-1855) who documented North American forest trees; author of the name Pinus australis.

label: Pinus palustris (longleaf pine)
summary: Longleaf pine of the southeastern United States, the chief source of American gum turpentine.

label: Pinus heterophylla (slash pine)
summary: Slash pine of the southeastern US coastal plain, the second great American turpentine pine.

label: Pinus echinata (shortleaf pine)
summary: Shortleaf pine, a widespread southeastern US timber pine and minor turpentine source.

label: turpentine (oil of turpentine)
summary: The volatile oil distilled from pine oleoresin or pine wood; the commodity whose American varieties this page characterises.

label: pine oil
summary: The heavy, high-boiling fraction obtained alongside wood turpentine from pine stumps, rich in terpineol, borneol and fenchyl alcohol.

label: Frankforter & Frary, Jour. Amer. Chem. Soc. 28 (1906), 1461
summary: Footnote citation of the 1906 JACS paper in which Frankforter and Frary examined pinene and the doubtful terpene 'firpene'.
canonical: G. B. Frankforter & F. C. Frary, 'The Chlor-hydrochlorides of Pinene and Firpene', Journal of the American Chemical Society 28, no. 10 (1906), pp. 1461-1467
